newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - Sanluis raised to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sanluis raised to buy.

text.p: Santander Investment said on Tuesday it raised its recommendation on Mexican conglomerate Sanluis to buy from market perform.
"Sanluis is attractively valued given an expected increase of 135 percent and 86 percent in normalized profits in 1998 and 1999, respectively," wrote Mexico City analyst Sandra Morfin.
Morfin said the company's auto parts division, Rassini, signed a contract worth an annual $65 million and should sign a brakes contract worth at least $26 million in additional revenue.
The company's mining division is likely to open a new mine by mid-1998 to double gold output, she said in a report.

"The stock trades at an estimated 1998 P/E of 9.1 times, and represents an unjustified 17 percent discount to its auto parts and mining peers," she wrote. Santander's 12-month $43.30 price target implies 23 percent upside, Morfin added.
Investment risks include a rising debt load to increase production capacity and still weak metal prices, she wrote.
Sanluis shares were up 30 centavos in midday trading to 46.20 pesos per share.
